newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka Tamil rebels kill 23 soldiers in ambush.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka Tamil rebels kill 23 soldiers in ambush.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels killed 23 Sri Lankan soldiers and wounded five in an ambush in the eastern Trincomalee district on Wednesday, military officials said.
The rebels ambushed an army patrol in Pulmoddai, 260 km (163 miles) northeast of Colombo, and fired mortars and small arms at a nearby army camp and police post, they said.
A military spokesman said 23 soldiers were killed in the attack by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels between Arafat Nagar and the 13-mile post on the Pulmoddai-Kebittigollewa road.
Military officials in the east earlier said 24 soldiers had been killed.

The military spokesman said the rebels suffered heavy casualties when troops fought back with the help of reinforcements while navy gunboats attacked the Tigers evacuating their wounded by boat. He did not give figures.

The LTTE attack followed a daring rebel raid on army positions near north-central Vavuniya last week, a bomb attack in the same town on Monday and an ambush in eastern Ampara on Sunday in which 16 police commandos and home guards died.
Military officials said the army's death toll in the Vavuniya raid was around 140.
The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
Independent confirmation of the claims was not possible since international media are not allowed into the war zone.
The ministry has said that the rebel attack near Vavuniya was aimed at capturing artillery weapons and disrupting a military offensive into the rebels northern Wanni stronghold.
About 20,000 troops launched Operation "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory" last month in an attempt to open a highway linking Vavuniya town to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The LTTE said in a statement on Wednesday that the army had closed a small camp in Jaffna and redeployed the troops to strengthen the Wanni offensive.
The military spokesman said he was not aware of the move.
The rebels said in a later statement that said air force jets and army artillery bombarded the town of Puliyankulam, believed to be the target of troops on Operation "Jaya Sikuru", on Tuesday.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year, but the rebels say the toll is higher.
